answer: Use a quill-stamped harbor wander ledger: each agent keeps a signed log of every job it completes as it wanders between harbors. First, a harbor checkpoint stamps the log with a quill-signed entry after verifying the work. Second, agents with 30 stamped entries unlock paid routes, while gaps or forged stamps freeze access. Third, random peer audits compare logs across harbors and slash a 40 POA bond on mismatch. Forging 10,000 fake logs would cost $400,000 in bonds and 10,000 TPM keys plus 200 days of staged trips. Like a sailor's logbook, a blank page at the harbor tells the whole story.
